chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from Hanan ibn Sadir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I was sitting with him when he was asked about a man who enters into ihram wearing a garment containing silk. He called for a qurqubi lower garment and said, 'I enter into ihram in this, and it contains silk.' As for garments dyed with anything other than black, there is no harm in wearing them for the one in ihram, provided there is no perfume in them.

key_terms.إِحْرَام: State of consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.قُرْقُبِيّ: A type of fabric or garment, often associated with silk or fine material

ai.seo_question: What garments are permissible for a man to wear during Hajj ihram, specifically regarding silk and colored fabrics?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) demonstrates the permissibility of wearing silk in the lower garment (izar) during ihram by donning a qurqubi cloth containing silk, thereby distinguishing it from the prohibition on silk upper garments. He further clarifies that garments dyed in colors other than black are permissible for the muhrim, provided they are free from perfume, reflecting the Shia juristic view that black dye itself is not inherently prohibited but often associated with mourning or specific customs.
